question.:question/problem: Which of the following diagrams gives the slope field at the points indicated for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=-2-(-2)xy?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We have to sketch the slope field at the points $(1,-1)$,$(2,-2)$,$(-1,-1)$.

To sketch the slope field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the right-hand side of the differential equation.

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(1,-1)}=-2-(-2)(1)(-1)=-4, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(2,-2)}=-2-(-2)(2)(-2)=-10, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-1,-1)}=-2-(-2)(-1)(-1)=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting up our points and drawing our line segments, we get the following diagram.

knowledge_point.title: Sketching the Slope Field of a Differential Equation at Some Isolated Points

question.:question/problem: Which of the following diagrams gives the slope field at the points indicated for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=1x+(-2)y?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We have to sketch the slope field at the points $(0,2)$,$(1,-1)$,$(3,-1)$.

To sketch the slope field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the right-hand side of the differential equation.

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(0,2)}=1(0)+(-2)(2)=-4, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(1,-1)}=1(1)+(-2)(-1)=3, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(3,-1)}=1(3)+(-2)(-1)=5.\end{aligned}
$$
